transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, I just can't seem to stop worrying. It's like my brain is stuck on overdrive, and I'm worrying about everything at once. I worry about my marriage, if I'm slipping up at my job, the bills piling up. I keep starting house projects and dropping them, and then I worry about that. Honestly, I just feel like I'm constantly worrying that I'm failing at everything—like I'm failing as a husband and a father. It's just too much.
How long have you been dealing with this constant worrying?

It's been about nine months now. I guess it really started when... well, when this big cloud migration project at work ramped up. And right around that same time, the arguments at home just started becoming a regular thing, too.
Over these past nine months, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy doing?

No, I don't think so. I still like doing the things I usually enjoy. I mean... it can be hard to actually relax and focus on them with my mind racing all the time, but the interest is definitely still there. I haven't lost that.
Have you struggled with focus and leaving things unfinished since you were a child, or did that only start recently?

No, this is definitely a recent thing. I mean, I've always been pretty organized and able to get things done. It's really just been since all this stress started about nine months ago that I can't seem to focus or finish what I start.
Along with the constant worry, have you noticed any physical tension in your body, like muscle aches, tightness, or soreness?

Yeah, definitely. I feel wound tight almost all day, to be honest. It's like my shoulders are just locked up and I'm constantly bracing for something. And sitting still... it just feels impossible lately. I catch myself pacing around a lot between my work meetings. Even when I'm at my chess club, I'll realize I'm just constantly tapping the pieces. I just can't seem to relax my body.
